fact_text: Pakistan's deferred oil payment arrangement with Saudi Arabia lets it take delivery of crude now and pay about a year later, which eases the immediate drain on FX reserves.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Saudi deferred oil payment facilities Pakistan used from 2019 onwards carried roughly 6% interest, and the last tranche was taken in February 2025 before expiring.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Converting short-dated external obligations into long-term contracts reduces the pressure on Pakistan's FX reserves, because concentrated repayments in a single year force reserve drawdowns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Developing borrowers can fall into a debt-financing cycle in which fresh loans are raised mainly to service interest on existing ones, which is the problem the UN Borrowers' Platform was created to address.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan was nominated to chair the Board of Governors of the IMF and the World Bank Group, a role due to be taken up in 2027, giving it a voice in those bodies' highest decision-making forum.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's automated production monitoring system installs cameras inside factories so FBR can verify declared output and sales itself instead of relying on company-reported figures, closing a sales tax evasion route.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Production monitoring cameras were already installed in sugar, cement, tobacco, tiles and fertiliser plants, with textile, packaged water, packaged juice and packaged milk rollouts still in progress.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An IPO on the PSX can be halted and withdrawn by the issuer when the regulator receives complaints about prospectus sales figures, unallotted shares without refunds, or subscription funds routed to partner rather than corporate accounts.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The company withdrew its PSX IPO after both book-building and public subscription had closed, following allegations of prospectus discrepancies and a thinly documented 2026 conversion from partnership to public limited company.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The chemical producer formerly known as Lotte Chemical Pakistan now reports under the name Noventra, so historical data must be matched across both names.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst describes UBL as Pakistan's largest bank by size.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan to Chair IMF/World Bank Board, IPO Controversy, FX Reserves New Record | Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani car assembly runs on a negative cash cycle: buyers pay booking advances before delivery, so the assembler funds working capital from customer money and even a small entrant can scale quickly.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Chinese CKD kits carry lower embedded technology cost than Japanese ones because Chinese makers build at far greater global scale, letting local assemblers of Chinese brands offer more features at a lower price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On the analyst's rough estimate, a roughly PKR 10 million Japanese-brand car earns the assembler about PKR 0.7-0.8 million, while Chinese-brand models average closer to PKR 1.2-1.3 million per unit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Auto assemblers should be judged on profit per unit alongside volumes, since a maker with fewer but higher-margin models can out-earn a higher-volume legacy player.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The expiry of Pakistan's Auto Policy 2016-2021 regime raises CKD import duties available to new entrants and is expected to change sales tax on hybrids and plug-in hybrids, which feeds straight into retail car prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: New Chinese-brand assemblers in Pakistan carry a larger share of hybrid and plug-in hybrid models than legacy Japanese brands, which wait far longer before launching new models locally.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani auto assembly is essentially fully import-dependent, so when high oil prices force the government to defend the current account deficit under an IMF programme, vehicle and kit imports are among the first items restricted.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Curtailing car imports is politically cheap for Pakistan because it cuts the import bill materially while leaving the large majority of the population unaffected, which makes autos a recurring target in balance-of-payments stress.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's approach to auto stocks is to model earnings under a severe scenario such as a 50% import restriction halving volumes, and only pay a price that would still hold up in that case.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst rates Sazgar's product franchise as strong because its Haval line spans petrol, hybrid and plug-in hybrid versions, a new SUV model has been added and the company has broken local resistance to Chinese cars.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst puts Ghandhara's truck franchise at roughly 60% of the Pakistani truck market, which he treats as a strong product position.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Atlas Honda dominates petrol motorcycles, but if riders shift to electric bikes without the company fielding a competitive EV product, earnings could stay healthy while the market awards it a lower P/E multiple.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When a technological shift is under way, the market pays a high multiple for expected future profits and derates companies seen as losing the shift, so a strong current earnings stream can coexist with a shrinking P/E.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Indus Motor's product position has weakened since Chinese brands entered Pakistan, though the analyst still sees it as the most established legacy assembler whose cars sell at a reliability premium.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Local gas wellhead prices are capped by the petroleum policy vintage the well falls under, with a maximum of about USD 3 per unit under the 2001 policy and about USD 6 under the 2012 policy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A windfall levy takes roughly 40-50% of the realised oil price above about USD 50 per barrel for the government, so Pakistani E&P companies keep only part of any crude price upside.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because gas prices are policy-capped and oil carries a windfall levy, a doubling of international crude does not double Pakistani E&P revenue, so one-to-one price-to-revenue assumptions overstate the upside.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Disrupted LNG cargo deliveries push Pakistan to lift local gas exploration and output, giving E&P companies a volume gain on top of a price gain; the analyst sizes the combined profit effect at roughly 25%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: OGDC and PPL each have more than PKR 500 billion trapped in gas sector circular debt, so a credible government settlement plan would be the single biggest value unlock for both.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani E&P stocks traded at price-earnings ratios of only two or three times despite large reported profits because those profits were accounting receivables rather than cash, so cash conversion drives the multiple.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To find the real beneficiaries of a crude rally, the analyst screens for the share of oil rather than gas in each E&P company's production mix, since gas realisations hit a policy cap while oil keeps capturing price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: POL has the highest oil share of production among Pakistani E&Ps, but its reserve life is short because the bulk of its crude comes from the Tal block, which caps the multiple investors will pay.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: OGDC combines a high oil share of output with a longer reserve life than POL, which the analyst treats as making it a cleaner beneficiary of higher crude prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The share price fall tied to the Reko Diq delay is already priced into OGDC and PPL, so any positive development, for instance linked to Saudi investment, would be incremental upside for both.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: If the government subsidises fuel instead of passing prices through, producers book higher profits but do not receive the cash, repeating the receivable build-up that crippled the gas chain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's key test of an oil shock is whether it turns into a macroeconomic shock, which it avoids only if the government declines to subsidise petrol and diesel and lets prices pass through.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cement cannot travel: its value per ton is low relative to road freight, so long hauls such as Karachi to Lahore are uneconomic and plants sell into their own region.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Higher diesel prices raise cement haulage costs directly, so producers must push through bag price increases to hold margins.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When global gas and LNG prices spike, gas-fired power generators switch to coal, global coal demand and prices rise, and Pakistani cement makers face higher fuel costs they must recover in bag prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A closed Afghan border removes cheap Afghan coal as a supply option for Pakistani cement plants, leaving them more exposed to international coal prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cement kilns can run on coal, petcoke or biomass, and a plant able to switch efficiently between all three protects its margin when any one fuel spikes; biomass is cheaper than coal.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: At the same bag price, a plant producing at PKR 600 per bag earns double the profit of one producing at PKR 800, so the efficient plant deserves roughly double the valuation and a cheap inefficient plant's discount is justified.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An announced expansion can still be delayed if conditions worsen, but an announced acquisition must be paid for, so acquisitions commit a cement company to higher debt in a way expansions do not.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Maple Leaf's move to acquire Pioneer Cement will raise its debt levels, since an agreed acquisition has to be funded regardless of market conditions.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst scores Maple Leaf top of his cement efficiency ranking because it can burn petcoke, uses a high proportion of biomass and can also run on local coal.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: DGKC has an announced expansion and scores lower on the analyst's efficiency ranking, mainly because roughly half its operating capacity sits in the South region.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: South region cement capacity sells a larger share into export markets, where profit per bag is lower than in the domestic North market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: DGKC has been raising the biomass share in its kilns, which the analyst credits with improving its plant efficiency and margins.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst saw Kohat, Cherat, Lucky and Bestway as the safer cement names because none had announced an expansion and all carried manageable debt alongside efficient plants.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst calls Lucky Pakistan's number one cement producer, with installed capacity roughly equal to Bestway's and an efficient plant base.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A State Bank policy making low-cost housing finance available at roughly 5-7% supports cement demand by funding flats and homes that would otherwise not be built.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To hold cement exposure through a coal price spike the analyst screens for three things together: fuel flexibility across coal, petcoke and biomass, low production cost per bag, and little or no debt.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In a sharp normalisation of fuel costs the companies adding capacity through expansion or acquisition become the biggest beneficiaries, while in a prolonged squeeze the low-debt efficient plants hold up best.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Middle East conflict prompts Pakistan to try to pull back remittances and investment held in the region, which if successful would flow into real estate and support construction materials demand.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Auto, Oil & Gas & Cement During Oil Volatility, Sector Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Small cement companies can run off-the-book sales that cut reported profit and hurt minority shareholders, so the analyst cross-checks revenue against installed capacity and industry utilisation to see whether declared volumes make sense.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Larger cement plants are generally more efficient, so smaller plants usually earn less profit per ton, though specific advantages can close that gap.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A cement player with only 3-5% market share can lift utilisation towards 100% without triggering retaliation, because large players would lose more from a price war than they would gain by punishing such small extra volumes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Older, smaller cement kilns tolerate high-sulphur coal, so they can burn cheap local Pakistani coal, whereas newer plants built for low-sulphur imported coal have much less tolerance for it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The quantity of local coal available in Pakistan cannot cover a large cement plant's requirement, so big producers must rely largely on Afghan or imported coal while small plants can run on cheap domestic supply.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A cement plant serving remote or thinly contested markets can break away from quota discipline more easily, while one sitting in a dense market that every plant supplies finds it much harder.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement's plant sits towards interior Sindh and sells into small towns such as Sujawal, markets that larger producers have little interest in freighting cement to.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement exited the cement cartel in the winter of 2023, which let it run its plant at full utilisation instead of a quota-constrained share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement sold roughly 30,000 tons of cement a month before its cartel exit and about 45,000 tons a month at full capacity, against a South region market of around 500,000 tons a month.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because the extra 15,000 tons a month Thatta Cement added was tiny against South region demand, rival producers had little reason to respond by cutting prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cement supplied to government projects falls outside the industry quota rules, so a producer with a high share of public-sector sales has more freedom on volumes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cement carries heavy fixed costs, so the analyst's rule of thumb is that a 50% rise in revenue with all else equal roughly doubles profit, because incremental volumes come at very high marginal margin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After leaving the cartel, Thatta Cement's sales rose about 50% quarter on quarter while industry volumes were falling, and its profits roughly doubled in line with the sector's operating leverage.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement switched from imported to local coal in early 2023, which the analyst says roughly doubled its earning power before the cartel exit added a further doubling.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement ploughed roughly PKR 1 billion of post-cartel profit into renewables, announcing a 5 MW solar plant and a 4.8 MW wind installation for its own use.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement's solar and wind installations should generate about 25 million units of electricity a year, worth roughly PKR 750 million of annual savings at PKR 10 per unit on the analyst's arithmetic.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Industrial users running captive gas power plants faced steadily rising gas tariffs under Pakistan's IMF programme, which pushed self-generating manufacturers towards renewables with short payback periods.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: By 2024 Thatta Cement traded at an enterprise value of roughly USD 70 per ton of capacity, which the analyst considered a decent valuation for a small producer given that running at 100% utilisation may not last.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: At its November 2024 corporate briefing Thatta Cement said it would sell Belarusian tractors in Pakistan, first imported and later locally assembled, targeting 5,000 units a year at about PKR 1 million profit each.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: If the tractor venture reached about PKR 5 billion of annual profit, against roughly PKR 2.5 billion from the existing cement business, the analyst estimated it could add PKR 35-50 billion of fair value on around 100 million shares.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani tractor makers typically trade on price-earnings ratios of roughly seven to eleven times because the assembly model is high-return, and the analyst uses about 8 times when valuing a new tractor venture.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Tractor assembly shares the high-return characteristics of car assembly: the assembly plant itself is relatively cheap, and customers pay in advance, so a solid product can run at very high return on invested capital.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan imported only about 2,000-2,500 Belarusian tractors a year on average over the prior decade, which made Thatta Cement's target of 5,000 units from year one look hard to achieve.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Belarusian tractor maker already supplies Pakistan through other partners, such as Shahzad Trade Links for high horsepower models, so Thatta Cement's subsidiary does not have exclusive access to that product line.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement's subsidiary already owns an old tractor assembly plant at Hub that it plans to reopen for local assembly, which could let it move faster than rivals negotiating fresh Belarusian partnerships.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement reported placing an order for 150 tractors, of which 27 had already arrived in Pakistan, a milestone the analyst suggests tracking to judge progress against the 5,000 unit target.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst could not verify the assumed PKR 1 million after-tax profit per tractor, since established local assemblers with around 90% localisation earn materially less per unit than that claim implies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The duty gap between an imported tractor and a locally assembled one in Pakistan is roughly 10-15%, so localisation can lift profit per tractor by that order.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: New industry set up in a Pakistani Special Economic Zone gets a ten-year income tax exemption, which is why most greenfield plants are sited there; reviving an existing plant outside a zone does not qualify.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Belarusian tractors are already established with progressive Pakistani farmers in imported form, costing more than local units but valued for durability; a 55-60 horsepower model runs around PKR 6 million.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement's earning power rests on selling 100% of production without disturbing the cartel, so expanding capacity from roughly 0.6 million tons a year towards 1.25-1.5 million would largely destroy that advantage.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement has been raising its stake in Thatta Power, but as the cement and tractor businesses grew the power stake became a smaller part of the group's overall fair value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Thatta Cement added a cement grinding mill expansion, which can raise near-term profits while adding to the volume that must be sold outside quota discipline.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's view of multibaggers is that fair value is re-rated in steps as successive developments land, so investors do not need to buy the bottom but do need enough knowledge to size each development quickly.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Selling as soon as a holding is up 30-50% is how most investors forfeit multibagger outcomes, because the company's fair value may be rising faster than the share price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Thatta Cement - Understand the Business Like Owners' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's cement industry has installed capacity of roughly 85 million tons a year against sales of only about 45-50 million tons, so the sector operates with large structural excess capacity.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A new cement line captures a share of national sales roughly in line with its share of industry capacity, so at about 55% industry utilisation a 3.3 million ton plant can expect to sell around 1.6-1.8 million tons a year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Efficient Pakistani cement plants earn operating profit of roughly PKR 4,500 per ton, which is the figure the analyst uses to value incremental volumes from a new efficient line.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: DGKC's average operating profit was about PKR 3,000 per ton in FY26 across its three plants, and the analyst assumes the oldest DG Khan site earns closer to PKR 2,000 per ton because its production cost is higher.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: DGKC announced a PKR 45 billion investment in a 3.3 million ton cement plant, the single largest unit expansion in Pakistan, designed to use more local coal and biomass than its existing lines.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: DGKC's new line both adds volume and replaces output from its old 2 million ton DG Khan plant, which the analyst estimates lifts operating profit by roughly PKR 10-11 billion a year before depreciation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On roughly PKR 10-11 billion of incremental operating profit against PKR 45 billion of capital, DGKC's new cement line implies a return on invested capital of around 25% at the operating level.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A greenfield cement plant in Pakistan costs roughly USD 60-65 per ton of capacity, so a 3.3 million ton unit would normally require about PKR 60-65 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: DGKC can build its 3.3 million ton line for about PKR 45 billion rather than the usual PKR 60 billion because grinding facilities, conveyor systems and other support infrastructure already exist at the DG Khan site.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The replacement cost method, asking what it would cost to rebuild the same efficient capacity from scratch, is the valuation approach the Pakistani market leans on most for cement companies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When valuing cement capacity on replacement cost the analyst counts only efficient plants and excludes units due to be shut, since obsolete capacity will not generate the profits the valuation assumes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Excluding the old plant it intends to retire, DGKC has about 8 million tons of efficient cement capacity across three locations, supported by captive coal power plants and solar investment.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: DGKC's value is not limited to cement: it also holds a sizeable listed investment portfolio made up mainly of MCB Bank shares.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: DGKC acquired a 32.7% stake in Rafhan Maize at PKR 800 per share, requiring about PKR 30 billion funded largely with a foreign currency loan of around USD 105 million priced at SOFR plus 3.25%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interest on DGKC's dollar loan for the Rafhan Maize stake will exceed PKR 2 billion a year against expected associate profit of PKR 2.2-2.5 billion, so the analyst sees little net near-term earnings impact.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The long-term logic of DGKC's Rafhan Maize stake rests on that company growing earnings through new products in Pakistan and on the pricing power its product range carries.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In a stable demand scenario with dispatches of 5.8-6 million tons, the analyst estimates DGKC can generate PKR 92-93 billion of FY27 revenue and, at a 25% gross margin, PKR 23-24 billion of gross profit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: DGKC also receives roughly PKR 4-5 billion a year of dividend income from its investment portfolio, which sits above the cement operations in the earnings build-up.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's FY27 estimates for DGKC exclude the new line entirely, because its earnings only start contributing in FY28.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst considers a price-earnings ratio of about 10 times defensible for Pakistani cement in a bull-market framework, a premium to a market trading nearer 8-9 times.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IMF-driven duty rationalisation cuts import protection for many Pakistani manufacturers, but cement is shielded because freight costs make imported cement uncompetitive inland in Punjab or KPK.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Budget 2024 additional limestone royalty left Punjab cement makers paying more than double the per-ton royalty charged in other provinces, a direct raw material cost disadvantage in a commodity business.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Punjab limestone royalty has gone to court and Punjab cement companies hold a stay, with managements sounding confident the inter-provincial royalty gap shrinks or disappears within one to two years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because DGKC's major plants and its new line are all in Punjab, removal of the provincial limestone royalty gap would help it most, though the analyst treats that as a potential bonus rather than a base case.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Budget 2026 reduced Pakistan's super tax, which mechanically lifts listed companies' after-tax profits without any change in their operations.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When LNG crosses roughly USD 20-30 per unit, importing countries shut gas-fired plants and run coal instead, lifting international coal demand and prices and raising Pakistani cement producers' fuel bill.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Developed economies peak electricity demand in winter for heating, unlike Pakistan where the peak is summer cooling, so the northern winter is when LNG and coal prices are most likely to spike.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the 2021 LNG spike and post-Covid energy super cycle international coal became very expensive, and cheap Afghan coal is what protected Pakistan's cement industry at that time.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With the Afghan border closed and domestic output too small to fuel the whole industry, Pakistani cement makers have less cushion against an international coal spike than they had in 2021.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani cement producers have historically passed coal cost spikes on by raising bag prices PKR 50-100, protecting profits until fuel costs normalise again.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats a coal price spike that depresses cement share prices as an entry opportunity, because the cost shock is cyclical and sector profitability returns once prices normalise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Nishat Group has bid for FESCO's privatisation; DGKC is not part of that bid today, but as a group flagship any change in the consortium structure would put it back in the news.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A distribution company privatisation is small relative to a large group's balance sheet, so its main effect on a listed bidder is attention rather than a material change in fair value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2025 template for the PSX was an improving geopolitical position after the India-Pakistan conflict, falling interest rates, a sideways phase in early 2025 and then a strong rally from July 2025 onwards.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's stated process is a three-step sequence of first understanding a business, then verifying the facts, and only then investing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'DGKC’s Rs 45 Billion Bet: Smart Expansion or Too Much Debt?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
